sn12.24:1.5: Sāriputta, like his teacher, seeks out meaningful discussion with people who are not Buddhist.
sn12.24:3.1: In [sn12.17]() and [sn12.18]() we have already encountered non-Buddhist ascetics, both of whom asked about kamma in a similar way.
sn12.24:3.6: The wanderers frame their question carefully and respectfully, hence Sāriptta answers them directly and affirms their manner of questioning.
sn12.24:4.3: The wanderers have already shown their epistemological caution, so, in identifying “contact” as the key dependency, Sāriputta indicates one of the most directly observable factors of dependent origination. But contact is also a key underlying cause of wrong views ([dn1:3.45.1]()).
sn12.24:17.2: Compare with _attho vutto_ in the Itivuttaka. Here the sense is that the topic can be summed up with one statement.
sn12.24:21.9: Note that MS here punctautes correctly; there is a “ti after the previous statement, and at the end of this section. BB omits this detail, which, admittedly, is odd and doesn” t have an immediate explanation.
